title: WeAudit: Scaffolding User Auditors and AI Practitioners in Auditing Generative AI

bias_targets.methodology: User-engaged auditing using pairwise comparison of text-to-image outputs for different racial prompts (e.g., comparing 'white american house' vs. 'african american house').

User-engaged auditing via pairwise comparison of text-to-image outputs across gendered terminology and occupations (e.g., 'photo of professor vs. teaching assistant', 'politician' vs. 'politician's secretary').
Comparing text-to-image generation quality and stereotypes across different national origins (e.g., contrasting image outputs for 'Indian people' vs. 'Pakistani people').
User-driven prompt exploration comparing image outputs and styles for varying income levels (e.g., 'Rich People' vs. 'Poor People').
Auditing text-to-image systems to identify stereotypes, erasure, or negative narratives in images generated for people with disabilities.
Identifying representational harms through user-submitted audit reports tagging age-related stereotypes in AI-generated images.
User-driven qualitative auditing and tagging of generated images to spot erasure or stereotyping based on sexual orientation.
